Can you explain the main options in simple terms?
Absolutely! Here's a simple breakdown of the main spirit types:
Whiskey - The broad category that includes several styles:
Bourbon: American whiskey made with at least 51% corn, giving it sweet vanilla and caramel flavors. Smooth and approachable.
Scotch: Whisky from Scotland, often smoky or peaty with complex flavors. Can be lighter or richer depending on the style.
Rye: Spicier, bolder whiskey with a peppery kick.
Tequila - Made from agave in Mexico. Ranges from fresh and citrusy (Blanco) to smooth and oak-aged (Añejo).
Rum - Made from sugarcane or molasses. Can be light and mixable or dark and rich with caramel notes.
Vodka - Clean, neutral spirit that's versatile for cocktails.
Gin - Flavored with botanicals (especially juniper), giving it herbal, floral notes.
Flaviar offers over 20,000 spirits across all these categories, from well-known classics to rare finds.

Good thinking! Honestly, you don't need much to get started—just the bourbon itself and a glass you already have at home will work fine.
But if you want to get the most out of your tasting experience, here's what helps:
The Essentials:
1. A proper glass (optional but recommended)
A Glencairn glass or tulip-shaped glass brings out the aromas and flavors best
Any whiskey tumbler or rocks glass works perfectly fine too
In a pinch, even a small wine glass will do
2. How to drink it:
Neat (no ice, no water) — best way to explore the flavors
On the rocks — use big ice cubes or spheres that melt slower so it doesn't get watered down
With a splash of water — can actually release more flavors, especially with higher-proof bourbons
That's it! You don't need fancy accessories or equipment. Just pick your bourbon and start exploring.

How do I use it properly the very first time?
• Just now
Seen • Just now
Great question! Here's exactly how to approach your first bourbon tasting:
Step 1: Pour & Observe
Pour about 1-2 ounces into your glass (doesn't need to be fancy—any glass works)
Notice the color—bourbon ranges from golden honey to deep copper
Step 2: Smell First (this is key!)
Bring the glass to your nose and take a gentle sniff
Don't stick your nose right in—the alcohol can overwhelm you
You'll pick up vanilla, caramel, maybe some spice—this preps your palate
Step 3: Take a Small Sip
Start with a tiny sip and let it sit on your tongue for a moment
Let it coat your mouth before swallowing
Your first sip might feel strong—that's normal! Your palate adjusts quickly
Step 4: Add Water or Ice (Optional)
If it's too strong, add a splash of water or a single ice cube—this actually releases more flavors and is totally fine
Big ice cubes melt slower and won't water it down as much
Pro Tips for Beginners:
Sip slowly—this isn't a shot, take your time
Don't worry about "tasting notes" on your first try—just notice what you like or don't like
Try it neat first, then with ice or water to see which you prefer
With Basil Hayden's at 80 proof, it should be pretty smooth and forgiving for your first experience. Enjoy the journey!
